observations: Two heads overlap at the center, each showing a row of bared teeth; the left head faces forward while the right tilts slightly, creating a doubled, crowded composition.
A dense web of crossing lines in yellow, cyan, red, white, and black covers the entire surface, with a hot magenta-purple field filling the background behind the heads.
A bold red angular shape—two strokes forming a rough chevron—sits high on the forehead of the left head, standing out against the yellow-orange mid-tone beneath it.
reading: Two heads press together, mouths open and teeth exposed in visible rows, their outlines tangled until the boundary between them dissolves. The magenta ground pushes forward rather than receding, so the figures feel compressed rather than floating. The red chevron on the forehead reads as a mark of pressure or alarm. The image sits somewhere between collision and chorus—two states of intensity sharing one space.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between nnxyz nifty faces #110 and nnxyz nifty faces #112 in both title and recorded creation order. Where #110 gives a single head room against a warm field, #111 doubles the figure and saturates the ground.

connections.reason: Both show a toothed mouth as focal point, but #110 places a single head against an open orange ground with a crown-like form above, while #111 doubles the head and fills every gap with competing color, making the contrast in density clear.

Both show multiple eye-like forms and bared teeth, but #112 arranges them in stacked near-rectangular blocks on a dark ground, trading #111's overlapping tangle for a more compartmentalized structure.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly do the outlines of the two heads separate, and where do they merge into a single shared line?
ambiguities: The red angular mark on the forehead could be read as a letter, a symbol, or a purely formal shape; no external evidence resolves this.
Title order and recorded creation order align here, but the metadata notes gaps exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so adjacency is not confirmed continuity.
